name: Wazuh
description: Open-source platform for endpoint monitoring, log analysis, configuration assessment, and security event detection.
strengths: Broad endpoint visibility; combines multiple monitoring capabilities; official documentation and community available.
limitations: Requires planning for agents, storage, tuning, and ongoing alert review; validate scale and operating-system support.
cost_model: Open-source self-managed; hosted options may be paid
deployment: Self-managed server and agents; hosted option also available
priorities: Security monitoring;Endpoint protection;Vulnerability management;Incident response readiness;Compliance support

name: Suricata
description: Open-source network IDS/IPS and network security monitoring engine for analyzing traffic and producing alerts and logs.
strengths: Flexible network visibility; rule-based detections; can support passive monitoring and configured prevention deployments.
limitations: Needs appropriate traffic visibility, rule management, tuning, and skilled alert interpretation; active deployment requires careful change control.
deployment: Sensor on a suitable network interface or traffic mirror; deployment mode depends on environment

name: Zeek
description: Open-source network traffic analysis framework that creates structured logs useful for investigations and network monitoring.
strengths: Rich protocol-aware logs; flexible analysis; useful as a source of telemetry for other systems.
limitations: Primarily provides visibility and logs; it is not by itself a general-purpose blocking firewall; requires log analysis skills.
deployment: Network sensor receiving permitted mirrored traffic or supported traffic input

name: Greenbone Community Edition / OpenVAS
description: Vulnerability assessment scanner and related components for identifying known vulnerabilities in authorized systems.
strengths: Supports structured vulnerability assessment and remediation workflows; community edition is available.
limitations: Scan results require validation; scan scope and timing must be authorized; deployment and feed setup can take effort.
cost_model: Community edition available; commercial offerings also exist

name: OWASP ZAP
description: Free, open-source web application scanner and testing tool intended to help teams find issues in applications they own or are authorized to assess.
strengths: Beginner-friendly quick-start materials; automation options; useful in development and CI workflows.
limitations: Testing must be limited to owned or explicitly authorized applications; automated findings need manual validation.

name: Trivy
description: Open-source scanner for finding known vulnerabilities and configuration issues across supported software artifacts and workloads.
strengths: Can fit into developer workflows; useful for checking dependencies, container images, and configuration artifacts.
limitations: Coverage depends on supported artifact types and databases; findings need triage and maintenance of CI integration.

name: Falco
description: Open-source runtime security tool for detecting unexpected behavior in hosts, containers, and cloud-native environments.
strengths: Useful for runtime visibility and rule-based detection in cloud-native environments.
limitations: Best fit depends on supported platform and telemetry; requires tuning to reduce noisy alerts and operational follow-up.
deployment: Agent/runtime sensor on supported hosts or cloud-native platforms

name: Security Onion
description: Open-source platform that brings together tools and workflows for network visibility, detection, and investigation.
strengths: Integrated learning and investigation environment; combines multiple security monitoring capabilities.
limitations: Can be resource-intensive; requires planning, tuning, and staff time for alert triage.
cost_model: Open-source platform; review current deployment and support options
deployment: Dedicated server or virtualized environment sized for the deployment
